chapter: Early records, Detroit and Prohibition-era nightlife
title: Playing and visiting the Cotton Club
summary: He filled in with a house band at the Cotton Club a few times and visited with Duke and Cab; he is unsure whether Black customers were allowed but walked in.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you ever play the old Cotton Club?
No. No. Well, yeah, I played in there a few times with just a fill-in band, you know, somebody to play up there awhile, to be the house band, that was off somewhere.
Now, did they not allow black people in there, customers, or did they just discourage them? Was there an actual rule?

Well, I don't know. I don't know whether to say it was -- discouraged them, I would say, I suppose, it was. Like I would say yes. But I don't -- I don't think they allowed them up there. No, I would say they wouldn't, no. But I went up there a few times, you know. I went up there a few times to see the show, you know.
So you could come in because you were a performer?

Well, I don't know whether they knew I was a performer or not, you know. I just walked in, you know, right straight in the front door and straight up the steps, you know. They had booths. It was a fairly nice place. I'd go there they had a band. I went there with Duke. I went there with Cab and whoever was there, you know.
